title: Interfaces
theory:
> **Curriculum:** This chapter follows [LEARN-LANGUAGES/CURRICULUM.md](../../CURRICULUM.md). Exercise ids are shared across LEARN-* repos for cross-reference.

## Interfaces

C# interfaces describe instance contracts; combine with **`switch` expressions** on types for polymorphic dispatch.

exercises.title: Define Interface
exercises.description: Define interface Shape with Area() float64 method. Implement for Rectangle. Create rect := Rectangle{Width: 3, Height: 4}. Print Area().
exercises.starter_code:
// interface Shape

record Rectangle(double Width, double Height);
hints: func (r Rectangle) Area() float64 { return r.Width * r.Height }

exercises.title: Interface Satisfaction
exercises.description: Define Writer interface with Write([]byte) int. Implement for Logger with fmt.Fprintln. Create Logger and call Write.
hints: func (l Logger) Write(b []byte) int { fmt.Fprintln(os.Stdout, string(b)); return len(b) }

exercises.title: Multiple Implementations
exercises.description: Define Shape interface with Area() float64. Implement for both Circle (with Radius) and Rectangle. Create Circle{5} and Rectangle{3,4}, call Area on both, print the larger area.

exercises.title: Type Assertion
exercises.description: Define Describable interface with Describe() string. Implement for Person{name}. Create interface var, use type assertion to get Person and print name.
exercises.starter_code:
record Person(string Name) : IDescribable { public string Describe() => "Person: " + Name; }
interface IDescribable { string Describe(); }

exercises.title: Type Switch
exercises.description: Create a function describeAny(x interface{}) that uses type switch to print "int: <value>" for int, "string: <value>" for string, "unknown" for other types. Test with both an int and a string.
exercises.starter_code:
// describeAny(42); describeAny("hello");

static void DescribeAny(object x) { }
hints: switch v := x.(type) { case int: ... case string: ... }

exercises.title: Interface with Slice
exercises.description: Define interface Speaker with Speak() string. Implement for Dog (returns "Woaf") and Cat (returns "Mew"). Create a slice of Speaker with one Dog and one Cat, then call Speak on each.

exercises.title: Empty Interface
exercises.description: Create a slice of empty interface{} containing: the int 42, the string "hello", and the float 3.14. Print each one's concrete type using a type switch.
hints: Loop with for _, item := range items
